assumptions: That the `monthly-spend-feature` flag was actually turned on at 15:22Z. This was inferred from per-minute evaluation counts in the service logs; the flag provider's change history was queried three times and reported zero recent flag changes, so no independent record of the toggle exists.

That the ZeroDivisionError path is reached only when the flag is on. The correlation in time is strong, but no code inspection or trace was performed to confirm the flag actually gates line 32 of spend_summary.py.

That no deploy was involved. The change channel returned zero deploys or releases for windows extending back to 2026-09-09; the buggy line must have shipped at some point, but the originating release was never identified.

Why the incident ended is unknown. No mitigating action was taken by the responder, and the last logs reviewed (15:28Z) still show the flag fully on with errors occurring, so recovery is unexplained by the retrieved evidence and may not be durable.
The baseline ~0-2% of account page failures from `UpstreamTimeout: payment authorization timed out` is pre-existing and was assumed unrelated; it was not investigated.
input.executive_summary: For roughly a minute and a half early this afternoon (15:27–15:29Z, with failures visible in logs from 15:22Z), a portion of customers loading their account page received an error instead of the page. Other parts of the shop were unaffected. The failures came from a newly active monthly-spend summary feature whose code crashed while calculating a customer's spend total. The automated responder investigated three times and consistently identified the feature's activation as the cause, but it could not confirm any recorded change to turn back, so no automated mitigation was performed and nothing was changed or undone during the incident. Errors stopped on their own at 15:29Z; the evidence gathered does not explain why they stopped, and the underlying faulty code was still live in the last log minute reviewed. The incident was escalated to humans with a draft code fix opened as a pull request (https://github.invalid/ohadraz/repository/pull/4) for review. The customer impact figure for this incident comes from the shop's own traffic measurements, not from this investigation.
input.root_cause: Account page renders on io-shop began failing with `ZeroDivisionError: division by zero` at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:32 starting 15:22Z, coinciding exactly with `monthly-spend-feature` evaluations shifting from 100% off to a mixed 121-off/79-on split in that minute and to 100% on by 15:23Z — i.e. the flag exposed a spend-summary code path that divides by an empty/zero denominator. Note this is an inference from the log evaluation counts: the flag provider's own history returned no recent flag changes, and the change channel recorded no deploy anywhere in the queried window (back to 2026-09-09), so the mechanism that changed the flag state was never positively identified.
